connections.why: Thomson's limit of 1862 on the age of the earth, "one of my sorest troubles" to Darwin, rested on the dissipation of heat that Thomson had argued for in 1852.

Jenkin's objection of 1867, that a single favorable variation would be "swamped by numbers" under blending inheritance, was among the hardest Darwin faced; pangenesis, his own theory of heredity, came the next year.
At Oxford Henslow, who had recommended Darwin for the Beagle, took the chair, and Robert FitzRoy, Darwin's old captain, rose to regret the Origin and was shouted down.
William Thomson's age for the earth's crust in 1862, most probably 98 million years, was aimed at Lyell's endless cycle by name, and Darwin called it "one of my sorest troubles."
